purpose: Dihydroergotamine is used to treat migraine headaches, sometimes with or without aura. It can also help treat cluster headaches. It works best when taken as soon as you feel a migraine coming on, but it is not used to prevent migraines from happening.
how_it_works: This medicine works by tightening or narrowing the blood vessels in your brain that become enlarged during a migraine. It also affects certain chemical messengers in your brain, like serotonin, that play a role in causing migraine pain. By doing these two things, it helps stop the headache and relieve pain.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting are the most common side effects. You may also notice tingling or numbness in your fingers or toes, dizziness, or a runny nose if you use the nasal spray. Some people feel flushing or warmth in the face. These effects are usually mild and temporary.
warnings: Do not use this medicine if you have heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or problems with blood circulation. It should not be taken with certain other migraine medicines like triptans or other ergotamine drugs within 24 hours. Avoid if you are pregnant, as it can harm the baby. Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, especially antibiotics or antifungals, as dangerous interactions can occur. Do not use more than the recommended amount, as overuse can cause serious blood vessel problems.
typical_dosing: The nasal spray form is usually one spray in each nostril, repeated after 15 minutes if needed, for a maximum of 4 sprays total per attack. The injectable form is given by a healthcare provider or as directed. Do not use more than 3 milligrams in one day or 4 milligrams in one week. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
